contests.title: Freeman Public Schools — School bonds and repayment tax

provenance.quote:
Shall Gage County School District 0034 (Freeman Public Schools) in the State of Nebraska issue its
bonds in a total principal amount not to exceed $13,995,000 for purposes of ﬁnancing the costs of (a)
constructing a new building on the District’s existing campus that will include career and trades
education and additional classroom areas, (b) renovating portions of the existing school building,
including the expansion of the current kitchen and repurposing certain classrooms and areas in
connection with the construction of the new building, and (c) purchasing certain necessary
equipment, furniture and apparatus for such new building and renovations, and making related site
improvements; said bonds to be issued from time to time, to be sold at such prices, to bear interest at
such rates, to become due at such times, and to have such other terms and provisions, all as may be
ﬁxed and determined by the Board of Education of the District; and

Shall the District cause to be levied and collected annually a special levy of taxes against all the
taxable property in the District sufﬁcient in rate and amount to pay the principal of, the premium, if
any, and the interest on said bonds as the same become due?

use tax upon the same transactions within the municipality on which the State of Nebraska is
authorized to impose a tax, speciﬁcally, impose a tax of one and one-half percent (1.5%) for village
capital and infrastructure improvements including streets, utilities, parks, landscaping, beautiﬁcation
and tree planting.

The Village of Sprague, Nebraska proposes to impose a sales and use tax in the amount of one and
one-half percent (1.5%) upon certain transactions within the Village on which the State of Nebraska
and Village of Sprague are authorized to impose pursuant to the Nebraska Local Option Revenue Act.

Shall the governing body of the incorporated municipality impose a sales and use tax in the amount
of 1.5% upon the same transactions within such municipality on which the State of Nebraska is
authorized to impose a tax?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Lincoln to use annual state assistance under the Sports Arena Facility Financing Assistance Act for a volleyball complex owned by nonprofit N4VB and related infrastructure. Financing may include revenue bonds repaid from that state assistance.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the project and allocation of state assistance.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this project and funding allocation through this question.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Changes the city charter to align city elections with statewide elections starting in 2028. Mayor and district council elections would occur in both 2027 and 2028; at-large council members elected in 2025 would serve until successors are elected in 2030. Transition terms would count as four-year terms toward term limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this election schedule and transition rules.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this proposed schedule and transition rules.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Offers the city’s alternative charter change aligning city elections with statewide elections starting in 2030. Mayor and district council elections would occur in both 2027 and 2030, and at-large council elections in both 2029 and 2032. Transition terms would count as four-year terms toward term limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this alternative election schedule and transition rules.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this alternative schedule and transition rules.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Changes the city charter to limit council members to two consecutive four-year terms, or eight consecutive years.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this proposed term limit.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Offers the city’s alternative charter change limiting council members to three consecutive four-year terms, or twelve consecutive years.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this alternative term limit.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Changes the city charter to let citizens who live outside city limits but within Lincoln’s three-mile zoning jurisdiction vote in city elections.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Allow these residents outside the city limits to vote in city elections.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this expansion of city voting eligibility.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes up to $13.995 million in school bonds for a new building with career and trades education and classrooms, renovations including kitchen expansion, equipment and site improvements. Also authorizes an annual property-tax levy sufficient to repay principal, interest and any premium on the bonds.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the school bonds and the tax levy to repay them.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize these bonds and repayment tax levy.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes a 1.5% village sales and use tax on transactions taxable by the state, for capital and infrastructure improvements including streets, utilities, parks, landscaping, beautification and tree planting.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the proposed 1.5% sales and use tax.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this proposed tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes a 1.5% village sales and use tax on the same types of transactions that the state may tax.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the proposed 1.5% sales and use tax.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this proposed tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Asks whether to remove Amanda Fangmeier from the Village of Denton Board of Trustees.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Remove Amanda Fangmeier from that office.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep Amanda Fangmeier in that office.
